pages.text: Contact Us - Data.gov Skip to main content An official website of the United States government Here's how you know Here's how you know The .gov means it's official. Federal government websites often end in .gov or .mil. Before sharing sensitive information, make sure you're on a federal government site. The site is secure. The https:// ensures that you are connecting to the official website and that any information you provide is encrypted and transmitted securely. Try the next-generation Data Catalog at catalog.data.gov and help shape it with your feedback. Data.gov is a metadata catalog. We provide information about federal datasets and links to where data is published. We do not own or manage the underlying data. If you have a question about a specific dataset, the publishing agency is the right contact. See the links below for answers to common questions before reaching out. Find and search for data # Search the full catalog at catalog.data.gov . Use the filters on the right side of the catalog to narrow results by geography, keyword, organization, publisher, or geospatial vs. non-geospatial data. Note: "Organizations" includes federal agencies as well as non-federal entities such as states and cities. Click any keyword tag on a dataset page to search for similar datasets. Many dataset pages include a link to the publishing agency's own landing page, which may provide additional context about the data. Data.gov links to data hosted by federal agencies. Controlling Wild Rodent Infestations Apr. 8, 2024 What to know Rodents can carry many diseases that can spread directly or indirectly to people. It's easier to control rodents before they can establish themselves in your home or building. Regularly check your home for rodent droppings and gnaw marks as these are both signs of a rodent's presence. Overview Rodents, such as rats, mice, and chipmunks, are known to carry many diseases. These diseases can spread to people directly, through: Handling of rodents Contact with rodent droppings (poop), urine, or saliva Rodent bites Rodent droppings, urine, and saliva can spread by breathing in air or eating food that is contaminated with rodent waste. Rodents can also carry ticks, mites, or fleas that can spread diseases. Many diseases do not cause any apparent illness in rodents. This means you cannot tell if a rodent is carrying a disease just by looking at it. Infestation of rodents in and around the home is the main reason disease spreads from rodents to people. Three months after his wedding, Faisal Shahzad's home in rural Punjab is bursting with gifts from his bride's family, as part of the dowry. But the most prized possession is tucked under the bed: a 340W solar panel. "In the summer we ran it from 08:00 in the morning until the evening," he says, adding they didn't need to use grid power at all during the day. "We ran our air cooler on it all day." Pakistan has seen a boom in imported solar panels, which glisten from the rooftops of homes and hospitals; from farmers' fields to industrial complexes. From 2018 to 2025, the share of electricity generated from solar energy in the country rose from 1% to 28%, according to Pakistan-based think tank Renewables First, with some seven million households now owning panels. People used to gift motorbikes or other household items at weddings, Shahzad says. "Now they give a solar panel and an air cooler. It has almost become a must." pages.description: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.
pages.text: Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google George Wright and Helen Davidson Watch: US ground stop caused by issue during copper wire update, transport secretary says A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations and prompted travel chaos was caused by a technical issue following a copper wire upgrade, the transport secretary has said. Sean Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem that led to air traffic controllers suspending take-offs for four hours on Friday had been caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades or faulty equipment. Though the ground stop was lifted on Friday evening, it had a knock-on effect on air travel on Saturday as airlines attempted to clear a backlog of flights. Officials including Duffy had previously attributed the issue to outdated equipment. Maintenance on US air traffic control systems was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre-optic cable by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider, Duffy said. The US had "an incredibly old telecommunications system", he said, adding: "It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued." Gardaí (Irish police) said the man sustained critical wounds during the assault at Lower Glanmire Road at about 13:30 local time on Tuesday, which Irish broadcaster RTÉ has reported was a stabbing. He was transferred to Cork University Hospital for urgent medical attention, where he later died. Two males, an adult teenager and a juvenile, have been arrested in connection with the investigation, gardai said. A post-mortem will be carried out on Wednesday at Cork University Hospital. Robins and bluebirds may be able to hybridize (there are no documented cases), but they have different plumages, songs, foraging habits and nest types, so it would be unlikely for them to choose each other. Such differences, along with geographic range and habitat preferences, prevent species from interbreeding even when it’s possible. Some species, like mallard ducks, do hybridize frequently. But the hybrid young may be a “dead end,” since they may be less likely to survive to adulthood or find their own mates. However, some lab groups and individuals hope to “bring back” extinct animals—including mammals, birds and amphibians—by modifying the genome of an existing species so the animal resembles an extinct relative and plays a similar ecological role. Knowable Magazine Schizophrenia is tough to diagnose. Patients may present with hallucinations (sometimes), social withdrawal (maybe) or delusions (not always). More generally, they just sound unlike themselves. Clinicians rely on their expertise and subtle cues to determine how different patients’ speech is, along with which symptoms appear over time, to justify leaning toward schizophrenia rather than another mental illness. This leads to delays in diagnosis. Americans with psychotic disorders—more than three million of whom have schizophrenia— receive a diagnosis a year and a half, on average, after their first symptoms appear. pages.text: Could T. rex swim? Kinda | National Geographic SCIENCE Could T. rex swim? Kinda Evidence suggests dinosaurs like tyrannosaurs were probably best suited to a version of the doggy paddle. Despite what's depicted in movies and books, the real Tyrannosaurus rex was likely an awkward swimmer at best. Illustration by Fotokita, Getty Images By Riley Black Published July 2, 2025 When Michael Crichton released the novel Jurassic Park in 1990, he included a terrifying chase through one of the park’s ponds. Fictional paleontologist Alan Grant, looking after kids Lex and Tim, tries to sneak by a dozing Tyrannosaurus rex and motor across a lake away from the dinosaur. The T. rex follows, swimming after them like “the biggest crocodile in the world.” The scene stood out so much that it’s been revamped for the new movie Jurassic World: Rebirth . But while tyrannosaurs might swim in movies and books, could they swim in real life? Carnivorous dinosaurs are not generally thought of as good swimmers. During much of the 20 th century, in fact, paleontologists wrongly assumed that herbivorous dinosaurs ran into rivers and lakes to avoid the jaws of T. rex , Allosaurus , and other predators. No one had found any direct evidence that such carnivores could swim. But the discovery of dinosaur swim tracks at fossil sites around the world have indicated that theropod dinosaurs—the group that contains T. rex , birds, and their relatives—were more aquatically adept than suspected and may have even done their own version of the doggy paddle. The Great Bubble Barrier Amsterdam’s Westerdok looks like many other outlets to the city’s historic canals. But look past the familiar boats and birds, and there is a distinct pattern in the water not found elsewhere in the city: a diagonal line of whiter water. That’s because an innovative “curtain,” known technically as a Bubble Barrier, lies below the surface. On the bottom of the waterway is a perforated tube which pumps air out, directing plastic to the surface. The natural flow of water then carries plastic litter to the Bubble Barrier’s catchment system, an aluminum trap on one side of the waterway, to prevent it from making its way to the North Sea. “Anything you can think of that people have in the city, we’ve seen here,” Philip Ehrhorn, co-founder and chief technological officer of the Great Bubble Barrier , the company behind the technology, told me as we surveyed the barrier on a warm day in September. As an example, the thermal energy released during the 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens was enough to power the entire world for about two and a half days. The Court is currently conducting a pilot program in which members of the public may apply for Courtroom seating through an online lottery . During the pilot program, Courtroom seating will also be available to the public on a first-come, first-seated basis. Before a session begins, a line forms on the sidewalk on East Capitol Street adjacent to the Court building. Please do not hold a space for others who have not yet arrived. Seating for the first argument begins at 9:30 a.m. The Supreme Court Building will otherwise be closed to the public when the Court is in session. There is a police officer on duty to answer your questions. Visitors should be aware that cases may attract large crowds, with lines forming before the building opens. Obviously there are unavoidable delays associated with processing and seating large numbers of visitors, and your cooperation and patience are appreciated. Court police officers will make every effort to inform you as soon as possible whether you can expect to secure a seat in the Courtroom. pages.text: Coverage Measurement Coverage Measurement Skip Navigation Within About Coverage Measurement The U.S. Census Bureau has a long history of evaluating population coverage in decennial censuses. Formal evaluations began with the 1940 census. Almost everything we know about the size of the coverage error, trends in census coverage and differences among subgroups of the population comes from the Census Bureau's own evaluation programs. Two principal methods are used to measure coverage in censuses. One method derives coverage estimates from post-enumeration surveys using dual system estimation. The other method is called Demographic Analysis (DA). DA represents a macro-level approach, where population estimates are developed for the census date by aggregating various types of demographic data. A coverage measurement program is essential for measuring the effectiveness of any census, including the 2020 Census, in terms of data quality. It is necessary to produce coverage measures to determine if the goals for 2020 were met and to determine how future censuses can be improved. This web site and its links provide an overview of these two methods, documentation of their implementation in past censuses, and documentation of their use in the 2020 Census. Demographic Analysis (DA) Demographic analysis is a technique used to develop an understanding of the age, sex, and racial composition of a population and how it has changed over time. pages.text: CPS ASEC Redesign and Processing Changes CPS ASEC Redesign and Processing Changes Skip Navigation Within CPS ASEC Redesign and Processing Changes CPS ASEC Redesign and Processing Changes April 17, 2019 Collected annually, the Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC) is one of the most widely used socioeconomic surveys, and provides detailed information on income, work experience, poverty, health insurance coverage, and living arrangements in the U.S. In 2014, the CPS ASEC included redesigned questions on income (specifically retirement income) and health insurance coverage, followed by changes in the 2015 CPS ASEC to allow spouses and unmarried partners to specifically identify as opposite- or same-sex. pages.text: Craig Bellamy: Wales boss takes belief from Nations League campaign - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Craig Bellamy's Wales seriously tested reigning Nations League champions Portugal in Cardiff By Dafydd Pritchard BBC Sport Wales Published 17 November 2026 Craig Bellamy kept coming back to one word. Belief. His Wales side had just lost a fifth game out of six to finish bottom of their Nations League group. Bellamy would have been forgiven for feeling a little bruised. But there are ways of losing and ways of finishing bottom. Wales were fearless against Portugal, exhilarating in attack and proving they can compete at the highest level of this competition, even as they were beaten 3-2 in Cardiff. And while they were already consigned to the foot of the Group A4 table, Wales' previous performances mean they at least have the back-up of a relegation play-off in March to preserve their top-flight status. "Belief's the biggest one," Bellamy said when he was asked what he and his team had taken from this campaign. "Not just this game, but in general. We are beyond close to this level. We can more than compete at this level. "We demand and want to expect to be. Getting into League A is big for us, but also staying in A is going to allow us to develop. "You can only develop and improve by playing the best teams, and I felt we've taken another shift." IDAHO FALLS, Idaho — As Idaho Cleanup Project crews prepare used nuclear fuel for eventual shipment out of state, they are designing and building a first-of-a-kind canister handling tool considered key to success in this important project. In the Road Ready Demonstration Project, the crews will transfer the fuel from storage at the Idaho National Laboratory Site’s Irradiated Fuel Storage Facility into U.S. Department of Energy canisters. The handling tool is essential to safely move the canisters loaded with the fuel into additional protective assemblies, making them “road ready.” The assemblies will be staged onsite until they can be shipped out of state. pages.title: Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences - BBC Sport
pages.description: The 2018 scandal has resurfaced this month after Usman Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about the cheating plot.
pages.text: Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Cricket Australia hopes the 'forum' will help the sport move on By Simon Atkinson and Tiffanie Turnbull Sydney Published 18 November 2026, 03:52 GMT Updated 1 hour ago Cricket Australia has launched an independent "forum" for players and staff involved in the sandpapergate scandal to share their version of events. In a memoir released earlier this month, former player Usman Khawaja claimed the entire Australia team knew of the plot to tamper with the ball during a 2018 Test in South Africa, contradicting the investigation at the time. His comments have led to a bitter split among former and current players and have overshadowed the beginning of Australia's international cricket season. The forum was not a new investigation and there will be no new penalties, Cricket Australia said, adding that nobody would be forced to take part. However, chief executive Todd Greenberg said he hoped the discussions would allow the sport to "move on". "The game is genuinely hurting at the moment. It's not good for anyone," he said. "We need to find a path through and we need some time to heal." The sandpapergate scandal is often described as one of Australian cricket's darkest days and was a source of national shame.
